sources.section: Struct layout, software prefetch and page size
sources.entry: Cache-Conscious Structure Definition - Introduces and measures structure splitting and field reordering on real programs, the origin of hot-cold layout rules.

summary.title: Cache-Conscious Structure Definition
summary.one_liner: Structure splitting and field reordering can improve cache performance of data structures larger than a cache block, by grouping hot or temporally related fields.
keywords: how to improve cache performance of structs
takeaways: Splitting a structure into hot and cold parts lets more hot fields fit in one cache block.
Fields with high temporal affinity should be placed in the same cache block when a structure spans many blocks.
In five Java programs, structure splitting cut cache miss rates 10–27% and improved performance 6–18% beyond earlier reorganization techniques.
bbcache is a tool that recommends field reorderings for C structures; reordering fields in 5 active SQL Server 7.0 structures improved performance 2–3% in preliminary measurements.
summary.summary: This ACM SIGPLAN'99 PLDI paper by Chilimbi, Davidson, and Larus extends earlier cache-conscious data reorganization, which focused on placing instances together, to the internal field layout of structures. It describes two techniques, structure splitting and field reordering, aimed at structures comparable to or larger than a cache block. The authors report miss-rate and performance results from five Java programs and describe bbcache, a tool that recommends C structure field reorderings, with preliminary measurements on Microsoft SQL Server 7.0. The listing describes it as the origin of hot-cold layout rules.
